policiesSlide.title: Policy Summary
policiesSlide.description: This policy reflects the USC's commitment to the health, safety, and welfare of persons and the protection of property should an emergency occur. It applies to all USC employees and defines reporting contacts for different hazard types (fire, weather, flooding, safety concerns, violence, medical emergencies, and other incidents), assigns responsibilities to the USC, the USC Emergency Response Representative, acting supervisors, and managers, and summarizes basic Western procedures for fire/evacuation and situations of immediate danger.

useSlide.title: Key Takeaways
items: Applies to all USC employees; an 'emergency' is an urgent or critical situation, temporary in nature, that threatens or causes harm to people, the environment, property, or disrupts critical operations.

Different emergency types have specific reporting contacts: Fire (ext. 83300), Weather/Flooding/Power failure (ext. 83304), Safety concerns (ext. 80371), and Violence, Medical emergencies, gas leaks, chemical spills, and most other emergencies (911 - Western Campus Police).

The USC must observe Western's emergency-related policies, declare an emergency or close operations if Western does so, collaborate with Western's Emergency Response Team, and display emergency numbers by all USC telephones.

The USC Emergency Response Representative (a member of senior management) can declare an emergency and close operations, collaborates with Western's Emergency Response Team/Committee, maintains USC emergency policies and training materials annually, coordinates departmental continuity plans, and maintains a secure list of emergency contacts.

Acting supervisors assist the Emergency Response Representative and ensure the safety of their workers and work areas; managers train employees on operation-specific emergency and evacuation plans as part of job-specific orientation.

In case of fire/evacuation: raise the alarm from a safe area while evacuating, use stairwells, close doors and windows, and remain outside until authorized to re-enter by the Fire Department, Western Police, or Western's Emergency Response Team.
In situations of immediate danger: avoid escalating the situation, leave an unsafe area, or if safe evacuation isn't possible, seek shelter, lock doors, avoid windows, and call Campus Police at 911.
Only personnel trained and acting within their competency may transport ill or injured persons requiring emergency medical transportation.

slideOne.title: 1. SCOPE
slideOne.oneOne: This policy applies to all USC employees.

slideTwo.title: 2. DEFINITIONS
slideTwo.twoOne: 'Emergency' means an urgent and/or critical situation, temporary in nature, which threatens or causes harm to people, the environment, property of the University Students' Council or Western University or disrupts critical operations.
slideTwo.twoOneOne: 'The USC Emergency Response Representative' is a member of senior management.

slideThree.title: 3. EXPECTATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
slideThree.threeOneOne: Report to Campus Police (9-1-1) any emergency situation;

threeOneTwo.intro: Report any hazard or potential hazard as follows:
items: 1. Fire Hazard: Ext. 83300 - Western Fire Prevention
2. Weather, Ice, Snow: Ext. 83304 - Western Facilities Management Division
3. Flooding, Power Failure: Ext. 83304 - Western Facilities Management Division
4. Safety Concerns: Ext. 80371 - USC Occupational Health & Safety
5. Violence: 911 - Western Campus Police, as per the Discrimination, Harassment, and Violence Prevention Policy
6. Medical Emergencies: 911 - Western Campus Police, as per the First Aid Policy
7. Gas leak, Chemical spill, Fall arrest/high angle rescue, Entrapment, Motor Vehicle Incidents, and all other emergencies: 911 - Western Campus Police

2. Emergency Service Reduction or Closure
3. Transportation of Dangerous Goods
4. Hazardous Chemical Waste Policy
5. Safe Campus Community

slideThree.threeOneFour: Declare an emergency and/or close regular operations in the case Western does so;
slideThree.threeOneFive: Collaborate with Western's Emergency Response Team; and,
slideThree.threeOneSix: Display emergency numbers by all University Students' Council telephones.

slideThreeTwo.title: 3. EXPECTATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES (CONTINUED)
slideThreeTwo.threeTwo: The USC Emergency Response Representative shall:
slideThreeTwo.threeTwoOne: Have authority within the USC to declare an emergency, close regular operations, and report such actions to Western's Emergency Response Team;
slideThreeTwo.threeTwoTwo: Collaborate with Western's Emergency Response Team, and other members of Western's Emergency Response Committee
slideThreeTwo.threeTwoThree: Maintain USC policies on emergencies by annual review;
slideThreeTwo.threeTwoFour: Maintain the USC Health and Safety training material on emergencies;
slideThreeTwo.threeTwoFive: Coordinate each USC department's preparation of appropriate fire, emergency and business continuity plans; and,
slideThreeTwo.threeTwoSix: Maintain a list of emergency contacts in a secure location.

slideThreeThree.title: 3. EXPECTATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES (CONTINUED)
slideThreeThree.threeThree: Acting supervisors from each department shall:
slideThreeThree.threeThreeOne: Assist the USC Emergency Response Representative; and
slideThreeThree.threeThreeTwo: Ensure the safety of their workers and work areas during times of emergency.

slideThreeFour.title: 3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (CONTINUED)
slideThreeFour.threeFour: Managers will train their employees on operation-specific emergency and evacuation plans as part of their job specific orientation, incorporating each operation's individual emergency plan.
slideThreeFour.threeFive: Greeting of emergency response services will be done by the Western appointed Building Emergency Coordinator, as per the UCC's Building Fire Safety Plan.
slideThreeFour.threeSix: Emergency Equipment: The Western Fire Safety Service will maintain emergency equipment, as per Western's Fire Safety Procedures.

slideFour.title: 4. BRIEF REVIEW OF WESTERN PROCEDURES

fourOneOne.intro: Raise alarm from a safe area on your way to evacuate the building;
items: 1. Use stairwells to evacuate;
2. Persons unable to exit by stairwells should find a safe area and contact Western Police to share their location;

slideFour.fourOneTwo: Close any doors and windows in the area;
slideFour.fourOneThree: Remain outside until authorization to re-enter is given by the London Fire Department, Western Police or Western Emergency Response Team.

items: 1. Avoid escalating the situation
2. Leave an unsafe area:
3. Seek shelter where you are if safe evacuation is not possible. Lock doors and avoid windows. Call Campus Police at 911

slideFour.fourThree: Members of the University community should ensure that ill or injured persons receive prompt medical attention from qualified personnel. Members trained in first aid should render assistance to the best of their abilities. Because the care and transportation of the ill and injured require specialized training and equipment, all persons requiring emergency transportation to a medical facility must be transferred by trained personnel acting within their competency.

slideFive.title: 5. COMMUNICATION
slideFive.fiveOne: This policy will be explained as needed to workers through operation specific or task-specific training.

slideSix.title: 6. EVALUATION
slideSix.sixOne: This policy will be evaluated on an annual basis through the Continuous Improvement Plan.
